name: QTT Reference-Memory Composition Test
description: Six frozen interference predictions, independent calibration and a count-preserving memory test \[\mathbf g_*=(1,c_*,2c_*^2-1,c_*^2,1,c_*^2),\qquad c_*=\cos\pi{8}.\] Can a retained reference recover interference that two fresh references cannot? This prospective protocol freezes the signed coherence for six histories: null, single, shared forward, fresh forward, shared echo and fresh echo. The forward and echo memory contrasts are respectively minus and plus \(\sin^2(\pi/8)=0.1464466094\ldots\). The paper derives the complete reference-partition map, specifies 24 history/phase settings, preserves every raw attempt including loss, and separates source coefficients from independent apparatus calibration. It fixes a disjoint training sample, 2.4 million validation attempts, simultaneous finite-sample rejection and equivalence criteria, and held-out scores against explicitly declared comparators. A second, independently timestamped laboratory capsule is required before validation data are acquired. What the test establishes. A qualified joint pass validates this QTT optical construction and its reference-memory pattern in the specified apparatus. The matched controlled-unitary quantum-mechanical model predicts the same pattern with the same calibration and no additional fitted parameters. Therefore this benchmark does not distinguish QTT from matched QM or independently establish an absolute clock.
